content.title: Timberwolves vs. 76ers: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (4/3/26)
content.text: The Minnesota Timberwolves (46–30) face the Philadelphia 76ers (42–34) tonight in a late-season cross-conference matchup at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The Timberwolves are on the verge of sealing an automatic playoff spot. They enter tonight in sixth place in the Western Conference, with the Phoenix Suns trailing by 4.5 games. Phoenix has just five games left to play, but they own the regular-season tiebreaker with Minnesota. Minnesota comes in off a 113–108 loss to the Detroit Pistons — a competitive effort despite being without Anthony Edwards. Julius Randle led with 27 points while Naz Reid and Ayo Dosunmu added 19 each. Minnesota entered the fourth quarter with a one-point lead, but Detroit pulled away midway through the final period and staved off a late Timberwolves comeback. The Sixers, meanwhile, look to retain hold over sixth place in the Eastern Conference with four tough matchups ahead of them. They enter tonight with the same record as the Toronto Raptors, but maintain an edge in the standings by virtue of a tiebreaker. Philadelphia comes in off a 153–131 blowout win over the hapless Washington Wizards, powered by 39 points from Paul George, 28 from Tyrese Maxey, and a 23-point, 10-rebound double-double from rookie VJ Edgecombe. Philadelphia has the edge here with Embiid probable, while Minnesota faces a tougher turnaround on the road and uncertainty around Edwards’ availability. Prediction: Philadelphia 76ers 117, Minnesota Timberwolves 111 Injury Report Minnesota Timberwolves Anthony Edwards — Questionable (Knee) Jaden McDaniels — Out (Knee) Philadelphia 76ers Joel Embiid — Probable (Illness) Johni Broome — Out (Knee) How to Watch Timberwolves vs. 76ers Tip-off for tonight’s Minnesota Timberwolves-Philadelphia 76ers game is set for 7:00 PM Eastern / 6:00 PM Central at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia. The game airs live locally on NBC Sports Philadelphia and FanDuel Sports Network North. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month. Fans in the Philadelphia area can access the NBC Sports Philadelphia stream with a Hulu + Live TV subscription here. You can start with a free trial to test the service — keep it if it works for you, or cancel anytime if it doesn’t fit your needs.
